4 امرط الشَّعَرُ The hair attained to the time at which it should be plucked out; it was time for it to be plucked out. (S, K.) ―
-b2- امرطت النَّخْلَةُ (assumed tropical:) The palm-tree dropped, or let fall, its ripe dates (Jm, K) in a juicy, or sappy, state. (Jm.) ＝
-A2- امرطت النّاقَةُ وَلَدَهَا The she-camel cast her fœtus in an imperfect state, with no hair upon it. (IDrd.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
